title: Speculative decode integration playbook and acceptance criteria
body:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for landing speculative decoding into the serving runtime, with practical notes about kernel selection, scheduler interaction, KV cache mutation semantics, and a concrete model integration checklist (acceptance/rollback/metrics). Goal is to make rollout repeatable and safe for hosted and dedicated customers.

Scope
- Runtime-level changes: scheduler hooks, kernel preference table, trace points for speculative branches.
- KV cache: semantics for speculative writes (not visible to other requests until commit).
- Model integration: how to onboard a new model variant that enables speculative decoding (or changes decoding settings).
- Monitoring and rollback: metrics, dashboards, alerting thresholds, manual and automatic rollback triggers.

Design notes / constraints
- Speculative decoding means we issue tentative tokens ahead of full scoring to reduce tail latency. The runtime must ensure final outputs are consistent and reversible.
- We assume multiple kernel variants per model (FP16-fused, int8-quantized, long-attention fallback). The scheduler chooses kernels based on seq_len, batch packing, and cost/latency trade-offs. Speculative paths may prefer cheaper/approx kernels for proposals and richer kernels for final scoring.
- KV cache is per-request and normally visible only to the request's continuation. For multi-request sharing (prefix cache), speculative tokens must never be committed to shared prefix entries until finalization.

High-level flow (runtime)
1) Request arrives -> router picks model variant and candidate kernel set (based on model metadata + request hints).
2) Scheduler places a speculative job (low-cost kernel) into a speculative queue with a time budget (t_spec).
3) Speculative job returns proposals (k best tokens / token logits). These are stored in an ephemeral speculative buffer tied to the request id. KV writes produced during this step are tagged as speculative and kept isolated (speculative_kv/<request_id>).
4) Finalization step: either the main decoder (stronger kernel) re-scores proposals or continues autoregressive decoding from chosen speculative prefix. If finalization finishes within SLO, commit speculative_kv -> request's main KV (or shared prefix on success). If finalization diverges or times out, discard speculative_kv and fall back to conservative path.

KV cache semantics and APIs
- Speculative writes: KV entries are written to ephemeral namespace: speculative_kv/<request_id>. Reads first check speculative namespace then base per-request cache.
- Commit API: commit_speculative(request_id) atomically merges speculative_kv/<request_id> into request_kv/<request_id> (and optionally into shared prefix cache if the request is eligible).
- Abort API: drop speculative_kv/<request_id> and mark the request to redo with conservative decoding.
- Eviction: speculative namespaces have a short TTL (e.g., 60s) and are cleaned aggressively. Garbage collection must be lock-free relative to in-flight finalizers.
- Isolation requirement: shared prefix caches must only be updated by commits, never by speculative writes. This prevents other requests from observing speculative states.

Kernel selection heuristics (for speculative + final)
- If seq_len <= 128 and batch_pack_ratio >= 0.7 -> prefer fused-attn FP16 kernel for final; use quantized int8 speculative kernel for proposals.
- If seq_len > 512 -> use long-kernel (chunked attention) for both speculative and final; speculative path may use lower-precision math (bfloat16) if available.
- If hardware == A100 && occupancy < 0.6 -> run small speculative batch on separate stream to overlap compute.
- Heuristic: only enable speculative decode for requests where estimated token cost > X (i.e., long-running decodes) OR when historical p99 latency for similar prompts exceeds SLO.

Scheduler changes
- Add a speculative queue with priority slightly above background maintenance jobs but below hard real-time SLO-critical jobs.
- Support overlapping streams: speculative jobs should not block finalization kernels on the same GPU if finalization is in progress; use CUDA streams or equivalent.
- Admission control: enforce per-customer concurrent speculative slots to avoid noisy neighbor impact. Configurable via runtime policy flags.

Acceptance criteria for model integration (new variant enables speculative decode)
(Automated + manual checks before >5% rollout)
1) Functional correctness (automated):
   - Unit tests for speculative commit/abort semantics (simulated concurrent requests) pass.
   - Deterministic reproduction: for a seed set of 1k prompts, outputs after speculative path + commit equal outputs from conservative baseline within allowed divergence thresholds (see metrics).
2) Performance (automated + load test):
   - p50 latency improves or unchanged; p95 decreases by >= 5% in synthetic replay test; p99 improves or unchanged.
   - GPU utilization does not exceed baseline by more than 10% for same throughput (we accept moderate extra compute if latency improves).
3) Quality (automated eval + sampling):
   - Regression checks on eval set (500 reference prompts): automated metrics (log probability per token, repetition index, safety filter hits) must not degrade by > 2% absolute.
   - Human spot-check: 200 sampled sessions reviewed by annotators; pass rate >= 95% compared to baseline.
4) Stability (in-test):
   - No memory leaks for speculative_kv after 24h soak test.
   - No kernel selection errors or fatal asserts in logs.

Suggested metrics to track (system + quality)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for total request, speculative stage latency, finalization latency.
- Throughput: tokens/sec, requests/sec.
- Cost: average GPU time per token, cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
- KV metrics: speculative_kv hit rate, speculative_kv commit rate, speculative_kv abort rate, avg speculative_kv size, GC count.
- Kernel metrics: kernel_choice distribution, kernel-fallback-rate (times speculative kernel required final re-run on final kernel).
- Quality: automated regression score (composite of log-prob delta, BLEU-ish ngram changes for structured tasks, repetition-rate), safety-filter hits per 10k requests, user-facing error rate (invalid UTF, decode exceptions).
- Business SLOs: SLA latency SLO breaches, customer error rate, retry rate.

Dashboards and alerts (initial)
- Dashboard 1: Speculative health overview: speculative commit rate, abort rate, p95 reduction compared to baseline.
- Dashboard 2: Kernel stability: per-kernel latencies and fallback rate.
- Alerts: If speculative abort rate > 5% for 30m, trigger P1-ish slack alert. If p99 increases by > 10% vs baseline during rollout window, auto-trigger rollout pause. If GC backlog > 1000 entries, alert SRE.

Rollout plan (recommended)
- Dry run: run speculative code in passive mode (collect metrics but do not commit) for 24h against production traffic replica.
- Canary phase: 1% of traffic to the speculative-enabled variant for 12h monitoring the metrics above. Manual gate: review human sample and dashboards.
- Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 48h windows with 12h observation at each step.
- Full rollout: only after 72h of stable metrics at 20% and human audit signoff.

Rollback triggers and procedure
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - p99 latency increase > 10% sustained for 15m.
  - Speculative abort rate > 10% for 10m.
  - Quality regression composite score drop > threshold (configurable) over rolling 1h window.
- Manual rollback: runbook to switch model routing (console + api) to previous model variant, disable speculative queue, and run a full GC of speculative namespaces.
- Post-rollback: capture trace-level logs for impacted requests, run root-cause analysis within 24h, and re-evaluate heuristics.

Testing checklist (practical)
- Unit tests for speculative_kv APIs and merge/abort semantics.
- Integration tests: replay recorded production traces with enabled speculative path (compare outputs and metrics).
- Load tests: soak for 48h with synthetic traffic that emphasizes long-decodes.
- Chaos tests: simulate speculative kernel timeouts and ensure fallback to conservative path without request-level correctness violations.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Exact commit atomicity semantics when committing into shared prefix cache (we need to define conflict resolution for concurrent commits that target the same prefix).
- Backpressure: how to prevent speculative jobs from starving finalization work on busy GPUs — strict per-GPU speculative slot limits?
- Cost model: quantify cost-per-latency improvement for common workloads to inform whether speculative should be enabled by default per-customer.

Immediate next steps
- Implementation spike: Marco/Leah to prototype speculative_kv namespace and commit API (2 weeks).
- Scheduler hooks: Owen to propose minimal scheduler changes and admission control flags (1 week).
- Metrics instrumentation: Sofia to add commit/abort counters and speculative stage timings to tracing (3 days).
- Integration PR: open GH PR and link to JIRA INF-7812.

Notes to reviewer
- This is a working doc — expect iteration. Please comment in the GH PR and the Slack thread referenced in linked_artifacts. If you have strong opinions about commit semantics or kernel heuristics, add a short blurb under the "Open questions" section.
